title: Occupancy decay investigation: host->device copy alignment & CUDA graph interaction
content:
Summary:
This note documents an investigation into repeated occupancy drops (per-SM active warp collapse) observed in a subset of microbatch workloads. Symptoms included recurring tail-latency spikes and low sustained SM active warps between kernel launches. The behaviour is reproducible in our staging flamegraphs when the serving runtime interleaves many small host->device copies with short inference kernels under CUDA Graph capture.

Why this is interesting / risk:
- Reduced occupancy increases per-token cost and worsens tail latency for live traffic.
- The pattern is intermittent and workload-dependent (short sequences + many small requests), so it can silently affect low-p99 SLOs.

What we measured (experiment summary):
- Tools: Nsight Systems (nsys v2026.1) + Nsight Compute sampling counters, in-house lightweight SM activity sampler (kernel that uses clock64 + activeWarpCount per-SM via nvml-derived counters), and CUDA Graph replay traces.
- Config: A DL model serving path with microbatch sizes 1..8, sequence length 32..256, 2 concurrent streams. Captures run on p4d-like instance with CUDA 12.x.
- Key counters: achieved_occupancy (nsight compute), sm_active_warps (sampler), sm_efficiency, and cudaMemcpyAsync timing from host.

Observed timeline (typical run):
1) Host code issues a series of small cudaMemcpyAsync() calls from many request handlers (sizes: 1–64KB).
2) Kernel launches follow on the same streams; kernel execution times are short (~300–800us).
3) When CUDA Graph capture/replay is ENABLED, nsight timelines show "copy nodes" and "kernel nodes" collapsed during capture/instantiate which changes capture-to-replay ordering in subtle ways.
4) During some replays we observe SM active warps dropping by 30–60% for ~2–10ms windows, even though kernels are queued — this correlates with periods of consecutive small host->device DMA segments.

Root-cause hypothesis (synthesized from traces and counters):
- Small, fragmented host->device async copies create many DMA descriptors and micro-transactions on the PCIe/NVLink path. The GPU DMA engine schedules these memcpy operations and pauses compute progression during some phases (particularly when stream priorities and stream->graph node merging cause interleaving).
- CUDA Graph instantiate/launch merges nodes at capture time: multiple small memcpy nodes and kernels are replayed as a combined sequence. In some hardware+driver combos this causes DMA scheduling to be more bursty; micro-copy bursts momentarily starve warps (SMs see fewer active warps) while the HW DMA state machine serializes accesses.
- Additionally, short kernels with high register usage already reduce theoretical occupancy; any extra serialization or memcpy stalls push SMs below the threshold needed to hide memory latency, resulting in the observed occupancy decay.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Nsight Systems timeline: repeated short memcpy events immediately preceding occupancy drop windows. The GPU work timeline shows kernel queued/ready states while SM active warps drop.
- Nsight Compute spot samples: achieved_occupancy decreases during windows; stall_reason shifts to "memory_dependency/memory_throttle" type metrics.
- Reproduced locally by increasing the number of tiny cudaMemcpyAsync calls (down to 4KB each) — the occupancy drop amplitude scales with fragmentation.
- When cudaGraph capture is disabled, we still see fragmentation stalls but they are less synchronized and produce smaller occupancy collapse amplitudes.

Quick repro commands (how we captured):
- nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o run_occdemo ./run_microbatch_client --microbatch=1..8 --seq=32..256
- nv-nsight-cu-cli --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency ./target_kernel_binary --replay 1000
- our-sm-sampler: nvcc sm_sampler.cu -o sm_sampler && ./sm_sampler --pid <target_pid> --sample-ms 1 > sm_samples.csv

Mitigations tried (and results):
1) Coalesce host->device copies in the runtime into a single bigger cudaMemcpyAsync per request (staging buffer). Result: occupancy collapse amplitude reduced by ~60%, p99 latency improved by 20–35% on the microbatch-heavy trace.
2) Use pinned host memory (cudaHostRegister) for request buffers. Result: DMA overhead lowered and memcpy latency variance decreased; combined with staging this further stabilised occupancy.
3) Change stream assignment: isolate copy streams vs compute streams so copy nodes don't compete on the same stream priority. Result: mixed — helped in some driver versions, less effective with graph node merging.
4) Disable CUDA Graph capture for short-lived request paths. Result: removed the synchronized collapse entirely, but costs: ~5–12% CPU overhead and slightly higher per-kernel launch cost.

Recommended fixes (short and medium term):
- Short term (low risk): implement host-side coalescing/staging buffer for small inbound tensors. Use cudaHostRegister for hot buffers. Add a runtime option to disable graph-capture for sub-1000us kernels.
- Mid term (development effort): implement automatic copy coalescer in the request aggregator to group small payloads arriving within a 200us window and submit a single DMA (configurable). Add detection: when sampler sees sustained achieved_occupancy < 0.6 for >5ms, trigger an auto-fallback to non-graph mode for that route.
- Long term (research): collaborate with driver team to understand DMA descriptor scheduling under graph replay; measure whether larger alignment (e.g., 64KB chunking) is beneficial; profile on different HW (A100 vs H100) and PCIe vs NVLink topologies.

Action items and owners:
- Evan: ship a small runtime patch that adds staging-buffer coalescing for the hot path; feature-flagged and default-off. (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Marta: run a cross-driver sweep (CUDA 11.8..12.2) and record how node-merging affects memcpy reordering (collect nsight captures, GH-1291). (ETA: 1 week).
- Ravi: add an automated sampler-based alert (arg: achieved_occupancy < 0.6 && duration > 5ms) in the dev cluster; add a dashboard panel. (ETA: 10 days).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Exact hardware DMA scheduling algorithm under graph-replay is opaque — need to escalate to vendor support if behaviour persists after coalescing.
- Is there a trade-off point where coalescing increases latency for some workloads (e.g., adds head-of-line waiting)? We need microbenchmarks for latency vs throughput under coalescing thresholds.
- Could kernel fusion (reduce register pressure) alone eliminate the effect? Fusion reduces launch frequency but increases kernel time; need to test viability for each model variant.

Notes for reviewers:
- Repro capture set and sm_sampler binary attached in linked_artifacts (GHD-1291). The experimental branch with coalescer lives in GHPR#4846; please review for integration risks.
- This doc is intended as the canonical investigation note for this failure mode; if we validate coalescing as default, we should add a runtime knob in the console to tune coalescer window size per-route.

Appendix: rough microbench numbers (staging vs naive):
- baseline (no coalesce, no pinned): p50=1.8ms, p99=12.2ms, mean_sm_occupancy=0.68, tail_occ_drops/sec ~5
- pinned-only: p50=1.7ms, p99=10.1ms, mean_sm_occupancy=0.72, tail_occ_drops/sec ~3
- pinned + coalesce (single memcpy per request): p50=1.6ms, p99=8.3ms, mean_sm_occupancy=0.84, tail_occ_drops/sec ~1

If you have specific traces you want me to run (particular sequence length distributions or hardware target), drop them here or add to JIRA-3145 and I'll prioritize.

-- Evan
